svg.title: Which mutations were found in which sample of patient 1
svg.desc: Schematic of Gerlinger et al., N Engl J Med 366:883 (2012), Fig. 2B, drawn from the lab's table of that figure (gerlinger_patient1_raw.csv). A grid with one column for each of the 133 mutations, in the paper's order, and one row for each sample: M2b, M2a, M1, R4, R9, R8, R5, R3, R2, R1 and, set apart below, the two biopsies taken before treatment, PreM and PreP. A dark cell means the mutation is present in the sample and a light cell that it is absent (840 dark cells in all). A color bar above the grid divides the columns into four classes: ubiquitous (41 columns, present in almost every sample), shared primary (31, present in most primary-tumor regions and absent from the metastases), shared metastasis (28, the reverse) and private (33, present in one region or a few). Eight columns are labelled with their gene: VHL in the ubiquitous class; SETD2, MTOR and two KDM5C mutations in shared primary; SETD2 and KDM5C in shared metastasis; SETD2 in private. The other gene names of the original figure are left out.
